content: Chloramphenicol interferes with the metabolism of various drugs by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal enzymes, particularly CYP3A4 and CYP2C19. This interaction can lead to increased plasma levels or effects of the co-administered drugs, potentially resulting in enhanced efficacy or toxicity. Below are the detailed interactions and clinical recommendations for each drug: 1. Typhoid Vaccine (Live): Chloramphenicol reduces the efficacy of the live typhoid vaccine through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Administration of the vaccine should be delayed until the completion of antibiotic therapy. This combination is contraindicated. 2. Umeclidinium Bromide/Vilanterol (Inhaled): Chloramphenicol increases the levels or effects of these drugs by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or consider alternative therapies. 3. Vemurafenib: Chloramphenicol increases the levels or effects of vemurafenib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 4. Venetoclax: Chloramphenicol increases venetoclax levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or adjust the venetoclax dosage. In patients with CLL/SLL, co-administration with strong CYP3A inhibitors during the ramp-up phase is contraindicated. For AML patients, adjust the venetoclax dose and monitor for adverse reactions. 5. Vilanterol/Fluticasone Furoate (Inhaled): Chloramphenicol increases the levels or effects of these drugs by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 6. Vilazodone: Chloramphenicol increases vilazodone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase vilazodone plasma levels by 50%; reduce the daily dose to 20 mg. 7. Vinblastine: Chloramphenicol increases vinblastine levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 8. Vincristine: Chloramphenicol increases vincristine levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 9. Vincristine Liposomal: Chloramphenicol increases vincristine liposomal levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 10. Vorapaxar: Chloramphenicol increases vorapaxar levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 11. Abrocitinib: Chloramphenicol increases abrocitinib levels by inhibiting CYP2C19 metabolism. Start with 50 mg daily when co-administered with CYP2C19 inhibitors. If no adequate response is achieved after 12 weeks, increase to 100 mg daily. Discontinue if the response remains inadequate. 12. Apalutamide: Chloramphenicol increases apalutamide levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. No initial dose adjustment is required. 13. Artemether/Lumefantrine: Chloramphenicol decreases the levels or effects of these drugs by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 14. Atogepant: Chloramphenicol increases atogepant levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Reduce the atogepant dose to 10 mg daily when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 15. Axitinib: Chloramphenicol increases axitinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 16. Bazedoxifene/Conjugated Estrogens (Oral): Chloramphenicol decreases the levels or effects of these hormones by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low. Use caution and monitor closely. 17. Belzutifan: Chloramphenicol increases belzutifan levels by inhibiting CYP2C19 metabolism. Monitor for anemia and hypoxia, and reduce the belzutifan dose as recommended. 18. Bortezomib: Chloramphenicol increases bortezomib levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 19. Bosentan: Chloramphenicol increases bosentan levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 20. Cannabidiol: Chloramphenicol increases cannabidiol levels by inhibiting both CYP3A4 and CYP2C19 metabolism. Consider reducing the cannabidiol dose when co-administered with strong CYP2C19 inhibitors. 21. Capmatinib: Chloramphenicol increases capmatinib levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 22. Ceftriaxone: Chloramphenicol decreases ceftriaxone efficacy through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution and monitor closely, as bacteriostatic agents may inhibit the effects of bactericidal agents. 23. Citalopram: Chloramphenicol increases citalopram levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 24. Cocaine (Topical): Chloramphenicol increases cocaine levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 25. Conjugated Estrogens (Vaginal): Chloramphenicol increases conjugated estrogens levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely, as side effects may increase. 26. Diazepam (Buccal/Intranasal): Chloramphenicol increases diazepam levels or effects by inhibiting both CYP2C19 and CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely, as strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors may decrease diazepam elimination, increasing adverse reactions. 27. Doravirine: Chloramphenicol increases doravirine levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely, as co-administration with CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase plasma concentrations and toxicities. 28. Dronabinol: Chloramphenicol increases dronabinol levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 29. Duvelisib: Chloramphenicol increases duvelisib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Reduce the duvelisib dose to 15 mg BID when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 30. Elagolix: Chloramphenicol increases elagolix levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Limit the elagolix dose to 150 mg daily and the duration of CYP3A inhibitor use to 6 months. 31. Eluxadoline: Chloramphenicol increases eluxadoline levels by inhibiting CYP2C19 metabolism. Use caution due to incomplete information on eluxadoline metabolism. 32. Enfortumab Vedotin: Chloramphenicol increases enfortumab vedotin toxicity by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 33. Escitalopram: Chloramphenicol increases escitalopram levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 34. Estradiol: Chloramphenicol increases estradiol levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely, as side effects may increase. 35. Ethinyl Estradiol (Oral): Chloramphenicol decreases ethinyl estradiol levels by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low. Use caution and monitor closely. 36. Fentanyl (Intranasal/Transdermal/Transmucosal): Chloramphenicol increases fentanyl levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor patients for respiratory depression and sedation, and adjust the fentanyl dose as needed. 37. Flibanserin: Chloramphenicol increases flibanserin levels by inhibiting both CYP2C19 and CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely, as adverse effects may increase. 38. Fluticasone Furoate: Chloramphenicol increases fluticasone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely, as systemic exposure may increase. 39. Fosphenytoin: Chloramphenicol increases fosphenytoin levels by decreasing metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 40. Fostamatinib: Chloramphenicol increases fostamatinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 41. Gefitinib: Chloramphenicol increases gefitinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 42. Hydrocodone: Chloramphenicol increases hydrocodone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 43. Idelalisib: Chloramphenicol increases idelalisib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 44. Ifosfamide: Chloramphenicol increases ifosfamide levels or toxicity by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely, as ifosfamide may enhance the toxicities of myelosuppressive agents. 45. Istradefylline: Chloramphenicol increases istradefylline levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Do not exceed 20 mg/day when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 46. Ivacaftor: Chloramphenicol increases ivacaftor levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Reduce the ivacaftor dose when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 47. Levamlodipine: Chloramphenicol increases levamlodipine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor for symptoms of hypotension and edema, and adjust the dose as needed. 48. Levonorgestrel/Ethinyl Estradiol (Oral): Chloramphenicol decreases the efficacy of these hormones by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low. Use caution and monitor closely. 49. Lomitapide: Chloramphenicol increases lomitapide levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The lomitapide dose should not exceed 30 mg/day. 50. Lumataperone: Chloramphenicol increases lumataperone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Reduce the lumataperone dose to 5 mg/day when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 51. Lumefantrine: Chloramphenicol increases lumefantrine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 52. Maraviroc: Chloramphenicol increases maraviroc levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust the maraviroc dose to 150 mg BID. 53. Mavorixafor: Chloramphenicol increases mavorixafor levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Reduce the daily dose when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 54. Midazolam (Intranasal): Chloramphenicol increases midazolam levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor for prolonged sedation and adjust the dose as needed. 55. Mirvetuximab Soravtansine: Chloramphenicol increases mirvetuximab soravtansine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. This list provides detailed guidance for managing drug interactions with chloramphenicol. Always monitor patients closely for adverse effects and adjust dosages as necessary.
